videos.title: Why AI isn't going to become conscious
videos.focus: Independent neuroscience argument separating fluent intelligence from consciousness claims
videos.summary: Neuroscientist Anil Seth argues that intelligence and consciousness are different, language models invite anthropomorphic projection, and biological embodiment may matter to experience. The complete transcript presents a contested scientific position rather than settled proof. Its April date and consecutive-day TED exposure remain advisories; the exact program is archive-new.
videos.why_it_matters: Readers can separate observed model behavior from claims about subjective experience, ask which biological or computational assumptions support a consciousness claim, and avoid granting or withholding control based only on persuasive language.

videos.title: Will we be ready when AI goes rogue?
videos.source: PBS / Washington Week with The Atlantic
videos.focus: Independent debate about agent containment, oversight, attribution and public accountability
videos.summary: Jeffrey Goldberg and Josh Tyrangiel debate a reported agent-containment incident, weak supervision, regulatory capacity and beneficial AI uses. The complete official transcript includes dramatic analogies and disputed interpretations, so claims remain attributed rather than verified facts. The September date and consecutive-day PBS-family exposure are advisories; the exact program is archive-new.
